class.name: ICloud
class.brief_description: Files in the player's iCloud, on macOS, iOS and tvOS.
class.description: Keeps files in the player's private iCloud database through CloudKit. [Purr] uses it for saves when a player hasn't added an email to an online account, so games rarely call it directly. It's off until the game names its iCloud container in [code]icloud/container[/code] (such as [code]iCloud.com.example.game[/code]). The container has to be created for the app in Apple's developer portal and added to its provisioning profile, and the export preset must give the game these entitlements, in [code]entitlements/additional[/code] (iOS and tvOS) or [code]codesign/entitlements/additional[/code] (macOS): [codeblock lang=text] <key>com.apple.developer.icloud-container-identifiers</key> <array><string>iCloud.com.example.game</string></array> <key>com.apple.developer.icloud-services</key> <array><string>CloudKit</string></array> [/codeblock] A Mac game distributed outside the App Store also needs [code]com.apple.developer.icloud-container-environment[/code] set to [code]Production[/code]. Purr's export warns when the entitlements are missing. Every call returns a signal that fires once with a [Dictionary] with [code]ok[/code] and [code]error[/code], plus what the call returns.

method.name: is_available
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the game has an iCloud container, its entitlements give it that container, and the player is signed in to iCloud on this device. On macOS, a game run from the editor, or exported without the entitlements, has no iCloud.

method.name: list_files
method.description: Lists the files without downloading them: the result's [code]files[/code] is an [Array] of dictionaries with [code]name[/code], [code]modified[/code] (when it was last saved, in milliseconds since 1970, by iCloud's clock) and [code]metadata[/code].

method.name: load_file
method.description: Downloads the file called [param name]: the result has its [code]data[/code], [code]modified[/code] and [code]metadata[/code].

method.name: save_file
method.description: Saves [param data] as the file called [param name], replacing any file with that name, with [param metadata] (small, JSON-compatible) alongside it. The result has [code]modified[/code].
